column1: > Where every file in the package comes from. installer/validate.py and the
> release workflow read this and nothing else.
> id      the name payload.tsv uses
> repo    owner/name on github.com, or "-" for the repository being built
> ref     a full 40-hex commit, because a branch is not a pin, or "-" for a
>         repository that does not carry these files yet. A "-" ref is loud, not
>         silent: validate.py prints the source as unpinned every run, a --src
>         build takes whatever directory it is handed, and a --bin build has
>         nothing to take. It becomes a commit on the day the split publishes
>         the files there, and never moves afterwards.
> UNRESOLVED is a source with no verified published commit. A payload row naming
> it must be gated by a preprocessor variable in abstraction.wxs, and the
> workflow leaves it out of the package and says so in the job summary. It is not
> a placeholder to be filled in silently: somebody has to decide where that file
> is published from and verify its commit.
> localstores is abstraction-storage-over-local-stores, the layer whose
> go/cmd/inventoryd is the first optional provider feature. scripts/split.manifest
> carries no rule for that repository and published.tsv has no row for it, so it
> has never been published and its ref is "-": a --src build takes the directory
> it is handed, a --bin build has nothing to take, and abstraction.wxs gates the
> LocalStores feature out of a package that could not obtain the program. It
> becomes a commit on the day the split publishes it.
> panel is the control panel, published into openabstractions/abstractions as the
> module github.com/openabstractions/abstractions/monitor. The directory reaches
> that repository through scripts/split.manifest's "tree monitor monitor"; the
> tag a module in a subdirectory takes is monitor/vX.Y.Z. The release route
> builds its Panel executable from the module version in redist/tools.tsv.
> modelhost is abstraction-provider-modelhost, the layer whose go/cmd/modelhostd
> is the second optional provider feature. scripts/split.manifest carries no rule
> for that repository and published.tsv has no row for it, so it has never been
> published and its ref is "-": a --src build takes the directory it is handed, a
> --bin build has nothing to take, and abstraction.wxs gates the ModelHost feature
> out of a package that could not obtain the program. It becomes a commit on the
> day the split publishes it.
